newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Deutsche Bank, Russia prepare for Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Deutsche Bank, Russia prepare for Eurobond.

text.p: Top Russian finance officials said on Wednesday that the country would press ahead with plans for a long-awaited Eurobond issue worth at least 1.5 billion marks ($878 million), even though their personal political futures are uncertain.
Finance minister Alexander Livshits, part of the cabinet dissolved by President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday, said his career might lie in the hands of God and Yeltsin.
But, speaking in Frankfurt, he insisted that Russia was an attractive bet for emerging market investors.

Deputy finance minister Mikhail Kasyanov told a news conference at Deutsche Bank's Frankfurt headquarters that the bond issue made Russia a major player in the mark capital market. Deutsche Bank is co-lead managing the issue with Credit Suisse First Boston.

Georg Krupp, Deutsche's management board chairman responsible for Russia, said the expected Eurobond issue would have a volume of at least 1.5 billion marks and a maturity of seven years. Full terms were due later in the day.
The debut Eurobond was likely to be priced to yield between 350 and 370 basis points over Bunds (German government bonds), bankers said.
The issue is the latest in a series of German-Russian cooperations in the debt market.
Kasyanov said Russia had not finished looking to foreign markets for debt capital. Asked about further Eurobond plans, he said: "On top of the 1.5 billion marks we expect a further $2 billion."
Servicing the debt would not be a problem because of improvements in Russia's economic situation and its improved standing in international capital markets, he said.
The favoured currency for new issues was the dollar, Kasyanov said, followed by the mark and then other currencies. But it had not yet been decided in what currency any further issues would be.
Russia was a good bet among emerging market countries, citing its record of reform as an example of some of the government's achievements so far.
The government had introduced constitutional checks and balances, improved the legal and regulatory framework and seen most prices and foreign trade liberalised, he said.
Gross domestic product, which has long been shrinking, was on the way up because of lower interest rates and the fact that inflation and M2 money supply growth had been brought under control.
There was also strong interest among different Russian regions in organising credit, but the legal situation still required clarification.
Kasyanov said the central government would not guarantee borrowing by the regions.

Livshits said the shape of the new government should be known by the end of the week. "My destiny and the destiny of other cabinet members lies in the President's hands and in God's hands. We think that government should, however, be more compact and more mobile," he said.
Earlier this week, Deutsche Bank said it had been mandated by Vneshekonomobank to arrange a one billion mark credit package to finance German exports to Russia.
Late last month the Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom signed an agreement with an international banking consortium, led by Dresdner Bank, offering a $2.5 billion loan facility.
